messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired — PAGER: High error rate + model-shard-heartbeat-loss in us-central-az7. Severity: potential customer impact. Links: https://internal.redwood/shifts/1798765432, runbook: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/az-failover

pagerduty: Auto-page to @sre-anna (primary on-call), escalation scheduled in 2m if not acknowledged.

sre-anna: Acked. I'm on it. Quick summary?

incident-bot: Metrics: generation-api 5xx rate spiked to 18% in us-central-az7 over last 3m. Average latency 1.8s -> 3.6s. Logs show repeated "shard heartbeat timeout" for model-shard-189.

eng-miguel: Pulling logs now. See tail:
```
[2026-03-14T16:41:12Z] shard-189: heartbeat lost, last_seen=2026-03-14T16:38:02Z
[2026-03-14T16:41:13Z] kube: pod redwood-infer-189 OOMKilled
[2026-03-14T16:41:14Z] runtime: connection rejects from lb: downstream resets
```
Looks like an individual shard eviction cascaded. Not seeing infra NIC flaps in fabric metrics yet.

sre-anna: Runbook suggests immediate fallback routing if shard rejoin isn't within 5m. Miguel, can you validate capacity in us-central-az3 and az5 for shifting model-variant traffic?

eng-miguel: Capacity check:
- us-central-az3: spare GPU capacity ~ 28% (enough for burst)
- us-central-az5: spare GPU ~ 12% (limit)

I recommend activating routing fallback to az3 and enabling degraded-mode quantization on the fallback pool to reduce token cost and speed up spin up.

platform-lead-sophie: Approve cross-AZ shift. Confirm we notify customers and set TTL for the change to 30m unless we see errors.

support-james: Notifying customers now. Top impacted customers: AcmeAI (account id: 6789), Nimbus Labs (id: 3344), and a PLG customer using streaming endpoints. Support note ready: "We are routing traffic away from a degraded availability zone; expect transient errors/responses during shift."

acct-ops-lee: Notifying sales for AcmeAI and Nimbus. We'll offer targeted credits if downtime > 15m.

sre-anna: Executing fallback. Command:
```
# activate routing fallback to us-central-az3 and enable degraded quantization
redwoodctl routing set --from us-central-az7 --to us-central-az3 --policy fallback --degraded-quant true --ttl 1800
```
Executing now.

pagerduty: Acknowledgement recorded. Incident status: acknowledged by sre-anna at 16:42:05 UTC.

sre-anna: Fallback command returned success. Pushing routing change.

incident-bot: Routing change applied. Config id: cfg-az7-fb-20260314-01. Telemetry: new route in 12s, initial traffic drain complete in 96s.

eng-miguel: Metrics update: us-central-az7 gen-api 5xx down to 3.4% after cutover; overall 5xx across region down to 1.2%. Latency returned to baseline ~1.9s for most requests. No new OOMs observed on shifted nodes.

support-james: AcmeAI reports errors reduced to <2% and successful retries. Messaging sent to customers.

platform-lead-sophie: Good. Keep fallback active for 30m and monitor shard rejoin. If shard rejoins and healthy, we can gradually rehydrate traffic.

sre-anna: Agreed. Actions logged. Opening internal incident ticket INC-20260314-az7. Assigning postmortem owner: eng-miguel. Will include timeline and remediation (pre-warm capacity & improved shard eviction handling).

eng-miguel: Adding note: we saw pattern of pod OOM after continuous cache buildup; adding an immediate mitigations checklist to the ticket.

acct-ops-lee: I've patched AcmeAI support case and put a 15% credit hold in case of extended impact.

sre-anna: Handing off monitoring to night shift (oncall: @sre-lucas). If shard doesn't rejoin within 30m, escalate to SEV1 and consider full AZ failover. Closing this pager thread; continuing incident channel for follow-up.

sre-lucas: Ack. I'll monitor dashboards and will call if we see re-escalation. :phone: 

incident-bot: This thread will remain open in #incidents:us for updates. PagerDuty: auto-escalation window reset.

sre-anna: Final note — immediate customer-impact window: 16:38:00–16:43:30 UTC. Recording for SLAs. :white_check_mark:
